newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NBM-Amstel sees EPS up 10-15 pct after '96.
newsitem.headline: NBM-Amstel sees EPS up 10-15 pct after '96.

text.p: Construction firm NBM-Amstelland NV said on Tuesday it expected earnings per share to grow by 10-15 percent in the years after 1996.
"The perspective is that we should be able to increase profit per share by an annual 10-15 percent in the years after 1996, barring unforeseen circumstances," NBM said in a statement.
It reiterated its 1996 forecast of an at least 15 percent higher profit per share.
Profit increases in the years after 1996 will primarily be the result of integration of its activities in Trading & Industry, said the Dutch builder and trader of construction materials.
"For the construction groups, the profit growth can mainly be expected in road infrastructure and the expansion of rail activities," NBM Amstelland said.

Referring to its other businesses, the company said that real estate development could benefit from earlier purchases of strategically located building sites while its home construction arm would recover profitability.
"In utilities construction, we expect stable sales and a moderate rise in profits," NBM also said.
Any acquisitions will be first aimed at expanding the Trading & Industry business, it added.
